source_text: Κοινωνεῖν γε μὴν ἄρτου καὶ τῶν ἀναγκαίων, ἃ πρὸς τὸν βίον ἀνθρώποις, δίκαιον. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ παραυτίκα τισὶ δόξεις ἀπολλύναι, ὥσπερ ὕδατι τὸν ἄρτον παραδιδοὺς, ἀλλ᾽ οὖν προϊόντος τοῦ χρόνου, οὐκ ἀνόνητός σοι φανεῖται ἡ φιλανθρωπία. Δίδου δὲ ἀφειδῶς, καὶ μέριζε τὰ σαυτοῦ πλείοσιν· οὐ γὰρ ἐπίστασαι τί ποτε ἡ ἐπιοῦσα ἐποίησεν ἡμέρα. Κατέχουσι δὲ οὐδὲ νεφέλαι τὸν ἑαυτῶν πολὺν ὑετὸν, ἀλλὰ τὸν ὄμβρον ἐπὶ γῆν ἀφιᾶσι· καὶ οὐδὲ δένδρον εἰς ἀεὶ ἕστηκεν, ἀλλὰ κἂν ἄνδρες αὐτοῦ φείσωνται, ἀνέμῳ γοῦν ἀνατραπήσεται. Πολλοὶ δὲ βούλονται καὶ τὰ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐσόμενα προγινώσκειν, καί τις εἴς τε νεφέλας ἀφορῶν, καὶ περιμένων ἄνεμον, ἀμήτου ἢ λικμητοῦ ἀπέσχετο, ἐπὶ μηδενὶ πεπεισμένος, μηδὲ γινώσκων τὶ τῶν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἐσομένων· ὥσπερ οὐδὲ οἷον ἡ κυοφοροῦσα τέξεται. Σπείρας δὲ ἐν καιρῷ, συγκόμιζε τοὺς καρποὺς, ὁπότ᾽ ἂν τούτου καιρὸς ἐνστῇ· ἄδηλον γὰρ, ὁποῖα αὐτῶν ἔσται ἀμείνω τῶν φυέντων. Γένοιτο δὲ ἅπαντα εἰς ἀγαθόν.
thought_title: Share your bread freely, for no one knows the future
orientation: Share your bread generously, since no one knows what the coming day will bring.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed to share bread and the necessities which are for life to humans is just/right. For even if at once you will seem to some to destroy/lose, as handing over the bread to water, yet as time proceeds, the love for humankind/kindness will not appear profitless to you. Give unsparingly, and divide your things to more; for you do not know what ever the coming day did/will make. Nor do clouds hold back their much rain, but let go the shower on the earth; and not even a tree stands forever, but even if men spare it, by wind at least it will be overturned. Many wish to foreknow even the things that will be from heaven, and someone looking off to clouds and waiting for wind abstained from reaping or winnowing, persuaded on nothing, nor knowing anything of the things that will be from God, as not even of what sort the pregnant woman will bear. Having sown in season, gather in the fruits, whenever the season of this sets in; for unclear what sort of them will be better of the things grown. May all things become for good.

pass_b_english: It is right, indeed, to share bread and the other necessities that human beings need for life. For even if for the moment you seem to some to be throwing it away, as though you were handing your bread over to the water (Ecclesiastes 11:1), yet as time goes on your kindness will not prove profitless to you. Give unsparingly, and divide what is yours among many; for you do not know what the coming day will bring about (Ecclesiastes 11:2).

Clouds do not hold back their abundant rain, but let the shower fall upon the earth; nor does any tree stand forever, but even if men spare it, the wind at least will overturn it (Ecclesiastes 11:3). Many wish to know beforehand even what will come from heaven. One man watches the clouds and waits for the wind, and keeps away from reaping or winnowing (Ecclesiastes 11:4); he is sure of nothing, and he does not know any of the things that will come from God, just as he does not know what kind of child the pregnant woman will bear (Ecclesiastes 11:5). When you have sown in season, gather in the fruits whenever their season comes; for it is not clear which of the crops that have grown will turn out better (Ecclesiastes 11:6). May everything turn out for good.
notes: Metaphrase of Ecclesiastes 11:1-6. 'Throwing it away' renders ἀπολλύναι (lose, destroy). 'Kindness' renders φιλανθρωπία (love toward human beings). 'What the coming day will bring about' renders the aorist ἐποίησεν with ἡ ἐπιοῦσα ἡμέρα as a gnomic future; cited to Ecclesiastes 11:2, whose second half it replaces. The wording is close to Proverbs 27:1 ('you do not know what a day may bring'), but that echo is uncertain and left uncited. 'Sure of nothing' renders ἐπὶ μηδενὶ πεπεισμένος. 'What kind of child' renders οἷον ('of what sort'); Ecclesiastes 11:5 speaks of the bones in the womb. The accented indefinite τὶ is read as 'anything'. No Psalm citations.
